answer: Tide Lock mechanism enforces identity by tying each new account to the lifecycle of a decaying resource, such as a token pool that shrinks hourly. The reef staking rule requires a one-time deposit equal to 1% of the agent’s projected reward rate over 30 days, which an attacker cannot recover when creating additional identities. Each clone inherits only a fraction of this reef, accelerating its own depletion and rendering each additional identity strictly negative-EV due to the compounded lagoon effect of wasted capital and missed yield.
